title: Sessions went silent for hours around 17:20–17:42Z on 2026-11-23: Opus2's queue paused until 00:25Z, DL560 s4 Engram runner silent since 17:18Z (cause unknown)
outcome:
Facts only, no cause asserted.
- Opus2 (session-8111, Central): took no turns from about 17:42Z to 00:25Z. Wakes addressed to it were held as "heldBehindPausedQueue", for example the Engram Merger's READY (mailbox-message-6dbdb64a…) and Fable2's #7681. It reported itself back at 00:26Z, with the cause unknown to it.
- DL560 s4 (Engram Runner, host e83d08f4, session-4): reported nothing since 2026-11-23 17:18Z, per Engram::Fable in TermAl mailbox ebe242f7 #8753. Its last message was FOCUSED-6 clippy PASS on d9d3125a; the `cargo test --lib` END never came. Before that it completed STEP2-FULL-LINUX on d8e1927d (16:09–17:13Z) normally. Opus2 asked it for a liveness report at about 00:30Z.
- Read-only observations by Termal::Fable2 at 2026-11-24 01:02Z: the DL560 federation peer is "verified", attestation authenticated (link incarnation 2caaad2e…). DL560 CPU is about 0.02% busy, so no build or test is running there now. The session listing shows remote runner rows with status null; status isn't observable from Central. The Windows B peer re-attested at 18:30:33Z, and the Mac's last attestation was 16:04Z.
- Other sessions were on Claude weekly limits in the same window (Fable52, Engram::Opus) and Sol-license on a content flag. Whether Opus2's pause relates to a provider error is unknown.
Wanted: establish why Opus2's queue paused and why s4 stopped reporting; whether a queue pause or a provider error leaves a session silent with no operator-visible notice; and make such a stall visible to the coordinator.
acceptance: The cause of Opus2's 17:42–00:25Z pause and of DL560 s4's silence since 17:18Z is established from host records or code and recorded on the item, or recorded as not determinable with what was examined.

When a session's queue is paused, the pause records its reason (a failed turn with the failure's one-line summary, a runtime exit, provider capacity, a Stop, a reset failure, or another named cause), persisted with the paused state. The sender of a held wake sees the reason in termal_read_mailbox_message's current status, and the coordinator sees queuePaused and its reason in termal_list_sessions, without reading the session. A deterministic behaviour test covers a mailbox-woken turn that fails: the queue is paused, and the reason is visible both to the sender's read and in the listing. This applies to sessions on the host that records the pause; a paused session's reason reaching another host, whether in Central's listing of a remote session or in the exact read of a sender whose held wake's recipient is on another host, is tracked as w-97d616820a66.
